messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use Meloxicam long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking Meloxicam.
Do not use Meloxicam just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take Meloxicam after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using Meloxicam, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
Such symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.
Triples: [["Meloxicam", "increases risk of", "fatal heart attack"], ["Meloxicam", "increases risk of", "stroke"], ["Meloxicam", "has risk factor", "long term use"], ["Meloxicam", "has risk factor", "high doses"], ["Meloxicam", "has risk factor", "heart disease"], ["Meloxicam", "can cause", "heart attack or stroke in people without heart disease or risk factors"], ["Meloxicam", "contraindicated in", "just before or after heart bypass surgery"], ["Meloxicam", "contraindicated in", "recent heart attack"], ["Meloxicam", "increases risk of", "another heart attack after recent heart attack"], ["Meloxicam", "has overdose symptom", "chest pain"], ["Meloxicam", "has overdose symptom", "weakness"], ["Meloxicam", "has overdose symptom", "shortness of breath"], ["Meloxicam", "has overdose symptom", "slurred speech"], ["Meloxicam", "has overdose symptom", "problems with vision or balance"], ["Meloxicam", "has serious side effect", "stomach or intestinal bleeding"], ["Meloxicam", "has serious side effect", "fatal bleeding"], ["Meloxicam", "has risk factor", "older adults"], ["Meloxicam", "has symptom to report", "black, bloody, or tarry stools"], ["Meloxicam", "has administration instruction", "call your doctor at once if symptoms of stomach bleeding occur"]]
Relations: ["can cause", "contraindicated in", "has administration instruction", "has overdose symptom", "has risk factor", "has serious side effect", "has symptom to report", "increases risk of"]
Answer:

completion:
can cause: The subject drug may lead to the specific medical condition or event specified by the object entity in individuals who do not have pre-existing conditions or risk factors.
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used in situations or for patients with the condition or event specified by the object entity.
has administration instruction: The subject drug requires the specific action or instruction specified by the object entity to be followed by the patient.
has overdose symptom: The subject drug may cause the specific symptom or adverse effect specified by the object entity when taken in excessive amounts or under certain conditions.
has risk factor: The subject drug poses an increased risk or is associated with the condition or factor specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the specific serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
has symptom to report: The subject drug may cause the specific symptom or adverse effect specified by the object entity, which should be reported to a healthcare provider immediately.
increases risk of: The subject drug is associated with an increased likelihood of the medical condition or event specified by the object entity.
